summary: Round 5. All six round-4 findings verified fixed except the one round 4 explicitly did not require fixing (the duplicated tier-3/R15 paragraph), which is still present and is recorded here as a minor. The recurring class of defect -- a fact fixed in the SPEC and left standing in the backlog -- is gone: `lastCheckpoint`, `The lease also`, `O(1) page` and `startAfter` have no occurrence anywhere in docs/, and backlog M4.3 now carries an explicit prohibition against pre-adopting a checkpoint-pointer field. Scope reads 1-12 and acceptance criteria read 1-12 with every cross-reference (`scope item 5`, `criterion 1/7/8/9`) still resolving to the intended item. The 16 backlog rows are 1:1 with the SPEC task table and I found no fact on which the two files disagree. Every requirement in the requirements table has an owning task and no task serves a requirement absent from it. The cost lens is clean: the commit chain is one writer at 1/commitBatchInterval, the lease is ~0.33 PUT/s, checkpoints are one PUT per K deltas or T seconds, recovery is bounded to zero LISTs, and AC9 asserts the pod dimension specifically. Five minors, none blocking; rule 11 applies and fixing them is permitted and probably wrong at round five.

Minor (SEAL/CONTINUE unowned): FIXED. Scope item 7 (SPEC:140-144) and acceptance criterion 11 (SPEC:445-449) both exist and both demand golden files for all three shapes, the version bump, every reader/writer in the same commit and the ADR travelling with it. All three surviving numeric cross-references still resolve -- 'scope item 5' at :361 is commit batching, 'acceptance criterion 8' at :86 and :180 is failover time, 'Acceptance criterion 9' at :367 and 'criterion 9's pod dimension' at :493 is commit cost, 'Criterion 7' at :491 is ack-ordering, 'Criterion 1' at :492 is the 1,000-seed run. Backlog M4.5 and SPEC task M4.5 both carry SEAL and CONTINUE.

Minor (vestigial 'Checkpoints reduce that LIST's span'): FIXED. The phrase has no occurrence. SPEC:376-379 now reads 'the bound above keeps recovery free of LISTs entirely outside cold start', which is consistent with SPEC:295-296 and AC5's cold-start exemption.

Minor (backlog M4.0 silent on rounds 2-4): FIXED and, as far as I can check it, honest. The row records that rounds 2, 3 and 4 each found further majors, that every one was inside the previous round's fix, names the three successive checkpoint-discovery defects (circular cursor; a page-count bound 50 checkpoints fit inside; the mechanism deleted from the SPEC but left in the backlog), and records round 3's diagnosis and the recurring fix-one-copy failure mode. Cross-checked against the packet's open-findings list: round 1 was B1 + M1-M5, which the row states as '1 blocking + 5 major'; rounds 2/3/4 were R2-1..3, R3-1..3, R4-1, which the row's characterisation matches. I found no false claim. It is a summary rather than the exhaustive log round 1 got, but nothing in it is untrue, so non-negotiable 4 holds. Its own factual claims check out independently: architecture.md:86-90 defines exactly I1-I5 and testing.md:95 requires the simulation to assert I1-I5.

findings.title: The tier-3 / R15 paragraph is still stated twice, near-verbatim, inside one section
findings.failure_scenario: Round 4 noted this and did not require fixing it; it is still there. ':282-284' says '...and recovery is tier 3 of M5's fallback ladder, run by up to 300 plugin nodes against cost.md R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling. A scan breaches that ceiling at fan-out, not at M4's own scale.' ':298-301' repeats it: 'Recovery is also tier 3 of M5's fallback ladder, run by up to 300 plugin nodes against cost.md R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling. A discovery path that scanned would breach that ceiling at fan-out, not at M4's own scale...'. The second copy is residue of the deleted mechanism text -- it now sits AFTER the cold-start exemption, so the section reads bound -> mechanism-delegation -> cold start -> the bound's rationale again. The failure it invites is the one this task has hit four times: two copies of one fact, and a later edit changes one of them. If the ~1 LIST/s figure or the 300-node fan-out is ever revised, the odds are even which copy gets updated. Deleting :298-301 loses nothing -- the 'exactly the kind of cost bug that surfaces two milestones later' clause is the only text not already at :282-284.

findings.title: Two live SKILL.md files are named as carrying the stale I1-I4, given no exemption reason, corrected in neither, and owned by no backlog row
findings.failure_scenario: The completion-condition paragraph enumerates five stale I1-I4 citation sites and corrects exactly one (roadmap.md). ADR-0002 is exempted with a stated reason ('an ADR is a dated record'). The two research documents are arguably the same kind of record. But `.agents/skills/spec/SKILL.md:40` and `.agents/skills/review/SKILL.md:93` are live procedures, and the SPEC itself flags the first as 'the worked example M5's spec author will copy' -- i.e. it names the exact propagation vector and then leaves it open, with no reason given and no backlog row created. Verified against the tree today: spec/SKILL.md:40 still reads 'invariants I1-I4 across 1,000 simulation seeds' and review/SKILL.md:93 still reads 'Does a claimed invariant (I1-I4) actually hold under the failure it names?'. Concrete failure: M5's spec author copies the worked example and writes I1-I4 into M5's completion condition, reintroducing exactly the staleness this commit exists to correct; and a reviewer of M4.13 following review/SKILL.md checks four invariants against an architecture.md that defines five, dropping the one the corpus calls 'the one a plausible implementation violates by accident'. Correcting them here would widen scope beyond what M4.0's row states, so the right resolution is a one-line backlog row (or a cross-reference gate in the M0.20 family), not an edit to this commit.

findings.title: AC5's fixture is single-epoch, but the checkpoint prefix is per-epoch and recovery is by definition cross-epoch -- so an epoch-local discovery mechanism passes
findings.failure_scenario: The grammar at :269 is `ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch:016x>/ckpt/<seq:016x>.ckpt`, so the ckpt prefix is scoped to an epoch. Recovery runs when a NEW leader acquires the lease and increments the epoch, so the newest checkpoint is always in a PRIOR epoch's prefix -- the new epoch's ckpt prefix is empty at that moment. AC5 says only 'with a chain of >=5,000 deltas and >=5,000 checkpoints present, recovery issues no list at all', and the T1 test-plan row at :466 says only '>=5,000 checkpoints present'. Neither induces an epoch change. So M4.8 can choose a LATEST pointer written at `ctl/log/<slot>/<epoch>/LATEST` -- a straight reading of one of the three candidates at :290 -- pass AC5 and its test row green in a single-epoch fixture, and then in production either miss the checkpoint entirely or fall back to a scan of a prefix that grows with uptime, which is the exact breach of cost.md R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling at 300 plugin nodes that :282-284 exists to prevent. This is deliberately NOT a request to re-choose the mechanism -- round 3's deletion of the mechanism from the SPEC was right and should stand. It is one clause in AC5 (or in backlog M4.8) saying the newest checkpoint may live in an EARLIER epoch than the one being recovered into, which is what makes the criterion discriminate. If it is not added, M4.8's mandated ADR review is the only thing standing between this and the same defect rounds 2 and 3 both caught, in a fourth disguise.

findings.title: 'node' and 'pod' both mean ingester node in the section that defines what 'correct at the end of M4' means, while 'nodes' means OpenSearch nodes twenty lines later
findings.failure_scenario: ':60-62' reads 'A single-NODE deployment is fully correct at the end of M4 ... what a multi-node one lacks is the path from the other nodes to it', and the very next bullet at :68 reads 'at the end of M4 a multi-pod deployment is not yet correct'. Same concept, two names, adjacent bullets -- glossary.md's one-name-per-concept rule, in the one paragraph the SPEC itself calls 'the single most consequential thing about M4'. It is not caught by check-terminology.sh because bare 'pod' is not a listed deprecated synonym and architecture.md uses it too. The misreading it enables is concrete: the same document uses 'nodes' for OpenSearch data nodes at :283 and :299 ('up to 300 plugin nodes'), so a reader can take 'a single-NODE deployment is fully correct' to mean a single-OpenSearch-node deployment -- a completely different and false claim about what M4 delivers. glossary.md:19 gives the unambiguous term: 'ingester node'.

findings.title: Acceptance criterion 8 is the only criterion no task row builds
findings.failure_scenario: AC8 demands a specific measurement -- 'on the simulated clock, from lease expiry to the new leader's first committed delta' -- but no row in either task table mentions failover timing. M4.12 lists the injected fault classes, M4.13 is the 1,000-seed I1-I5 run, and neither says it produces this number. This is the shape of round 1's finding (1), where AC9 carried the $52/month claim and no task built commitBatchInterval; the fix then was to add M4.7, which is why every other criterion now has a visible owner (AC1->M4.13, AC2->M4.3, AC3->M4.6, AC4->M4.4/M4.13, AC5->M4.8/M4.9, AC6->M4.10, AC7->M4.11, AC9->M4.7, AC10->M4.14, AC11->M4.5, AC12->M4.1/M4.2). The failure lands at M4.15: check-milestone-verified.sh requires one evidence line per criterion, and the author of VERIFIED.md discovers at the end of the milestone that nothing measured this, with the choice of writing the milestone's last commit as a new test or quoting an unmeasured number. Half a clause on M4.12 or M4.13 closes it.
